answer: Before a large payout, a new identity docks in a small harbor, its limit near zero, climbing only with a verified history of completed work over weeks, each week earning an opal mark. The payout desk reviews the ladder weekly; a claim above its rung is split into small tranches, and a forged history forfeits the claim and bars the identity. An honest worker climbs by doing normal work, while 1,000 fakes would each need weeks of genuine history — a gap near 1,000 to 1. When one operator pushed fifty fresh identities toward big payout before dawn, each hit the bottom rung and was turned away.
